findings.title: Invoice detail casts route param to Id<'invoices'> instead of validating
findings.why_it_matters: The `as Id<'invoices'>` cast turns off TypeScript's guarantee that the id actually came from the invoices table. At runtime the value is a user-controlled string from the URL. A wrong table id or malformed string will not be caught until it reaches the backend (or worse, the cast could mask a cross-table id).
findings.suggested_fix: Introduce a small helper `parseInvoiceId(value: string): Id<'invoices'> | null` that validates the shape, or use Convex's generated validators. Return a NOT_FOUND screen when validation fails.

findings.title: New activity screen uses `as unknown as [string, ...string[]]` to force Zod enum types
findings.why_it_matters: The `ACTIVITY_TYPES` and `ENTITY_TYPES` const arrays are filtered and then brutally cast into the tuple shape Zod expects. This defeats type safety: if the source arrays are empty at runtime or the filter removes all elements, z.enum will throw at runtime. It also couples the screen to the exact array shapes.
findings.suggested_fix: Export proper Zod schemas (or TypeScript enums) from @crm/domain and consume them directly. The domain package should own the 'status_change is system-only' rule and the valid activity/entity types.

findings.title: toAuthSession uses loose `unknown` narrowing and spreads records into typed shapes
findings.why_it_matters: toAuthSession casts the Better Auth payload through `as Record<string, unknown>` and then spreads session/user into typed shapes. Any extra fields pass through silently, and the only required fields checked are id and email. This duplicates validation that already exists in @crm/auth/session.ts and is a place where future type drift will hide.
evidence: apps/mobile/src/providers/auth-provider.tsx:77 casts v.session and v.user to Record<string, unknown>
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the inline toAuthSession with the existing `isSessionPayload` / `toSessionUser` helpers from @crm/auth. They are purpose-built and keep the provider free of auth shape validation.

findings.title: exchangeConvexToken lacks explicit return type and timeout contract in its signature
findings.why_it_matters: The function is exported and installed as `setAuth` fetcher. While the return type is inferred as `Promise<string | null>`, there is no explicit type annotation. Combined with the lack of timeout, callers (including Convex's setAuth internals) have no typed contract for how long the function may hang or what error behavior to expect.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit `Promise<string | null>` return type and document the timeout/abort contract in the function's JSDoc.

findings.title: Mobile env type carries a server-only secret through the shared Env type
findings.why_it_matters: Mobile imports the full `Env` type from @crm/config, which includes `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`. TypeScript cannot prevent a future developer from reading `mobileEnv().BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` and logging or sending it. The shared type is not client-safe.
evidence: apps/mobile/src/lib/config.ts:5 import { parseEnv, type Env } from '@crm/config'
apps/mobile/src/lib/config.ts:27 BETTER_AUTH_SECRET stub passed to parseEnv
findings.suggested_fix: Introduce a `ClientEnv` type in @crm/config that omits server-only secrets and use it as the return type of mobileEnv().

findings.title: No explicit type for AuthContextValue action callbacks beyond inline definitions
findings.why_it_matters: The signInEmail and signOut callbacks are typed implicitly through the AuthContextValue interface. While correct, the lack of standalone exported function types makes it harder for tests or future screens to mock the context consistently.
evidence: AuthContextValue is the only source of truth for their signatures
findings.suggested_fix: Consider exporting standalone types such as `SignInEmailFn` and `SignOutFn` for easier mocking in tests and screens. Low priority.

residual_risks: The `better-auth/react` createAuthClient return type is not fully constrained to the configured plugins; call sites rely on inference. If plugin configuration diverges between web and mobile, type errors may surface late.
testing_gaps: Type-level test asserting mobileEnv() return type does not expose BETTER_AUTH_SECRET.
Type-level test asserting CreateActivitySchema input type matches the api.activities.schedule argument type.
